text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT 2155558888 - spike in kv-cache size + NCCL stalls detected on tensor-parallel pools (us-west-2). Auto-escalation to oncall-ml. Links: https://pager.redwood/INC-2155558888, metrics: grafana/redwood/kv_cache, logs: splunk/search?q=kv_cache+blowup

oncall-ml: I'm on it. Paging SRE and runtime. Initial look: continuous_batching backlog spiking, a single customer workload causing huge prefixes to be cached. Also seeing NCCL timeouts on tp-shard workers 3/8.

sara: seeing lots of 500s and 504s reported from infra because GPU workers are getting NCCL backpressure. Affected clusters: dedicated-usw2-g1 and private-vpc-acs.

mike: temporary mitigation idea — disable continuous batching for affected pools and roll back the recent batch-config change pushed in the last deploy (rollout id: r-2026-03-12-77). Will that reduce cache growth?

eva: svc/kv-cache runbook suggests setting kv.cache.max_prefix_bytes and reducing max_batch_size. Ops-runbook-bot, can you paste the steps?

ops-runbook-bot: Runbook excerpt: 
1) set continuous_batching=false for pool in rollout manager
2) set kv.cache.max_prefix_bytes=4MB (default was 64MB for that rollout)
3) restart kv-shard-daemon on affected nodes with graceful drain
4) monitor kv_cache_size and kv_page_fault_rate
Commands: 
```
# toggle batching
curl -X POST $CONTROL_PLANE/api/v1/pools/affected/toggle_batching -d '{"continuous_batching":false}' -H "Authorization: Bearer $SVC_TOKEN"
# limit prefix size
kubectl -n rw-runtime set configmap kv-cache-config --from-literal=max_prefix_bytes=4194304
kubectl rollout restart daemonset/kv-shard-daemon -n rw-runtime
```

ryan: I'll do the config toggle and monitor. Starting now.

incident-bot: :information_source: Update: AWS ASG health dips detected on dedicated-usw2-g1 (3 nodes) — autoscaler triggered replacements.

oncall-ml: Quick note — customer impact lookup: two enterprise tenants showing elevated error rates: AcmeCorp (chat endpoints) and NovaHealth (inference jobs). CS looped in.

customer-success: Copy. We opened INC-ACME-413 and INC-NOVA-221 and notified their on-call contacts. Acme is seeing 10-20x token latency and intermittent 5xx.

mike: After toggling batching on a test pool, kv_cache_size stopped growing and page faults dropped. Pushing same toggle to production affected pools now.

eng-runtime: Observed uneven KV shard partitioning across tensor-parallel ranks. One rank holding 80% of keys due to allocator edge-case after recent allocator refactor (commit a1b2c3). That is causing NCCL allreduce stalls when that rank has very large memory pressure. We're prepping a hotfix to the allocator.

infra-shift-lead: Good catch. Can we roll a targeted patch? Hotfix plan: 1) deploy allocator patch (kv_shard_allocator.patch) with guard flag kv.shard.strict_balance=true 2) restart kv-shard-daemon with rolling restart 3) scale down continuous_batching window until shard balance stabilizes

oncall-ml: Can you drop the patch to canary pool first? We need to limit risk.

eng-runtime: Pushing patch to canary (pool-canary-3). Patch diff: 
```
- // previous heuristic favored prefix-length only
- shard_id = prefix_hash(prefix) % num_shards
+ // new heuristic mixes prefix_hash and token_count to avoid hot prefixes
+ shard_id = (prefix_hash(prefix) + token_count) % num_shards
```
We also add invariant checks to detect imbalanced partitions and log them at warn-level.

mike: Canary patch applied. Monitoring shard_balance_ratio metric. At t+3m the imbalance dropped from 5.2 -> 1.3 in the canary pool. NCCL timeouts stopped for canary workers. Rolling to production in 2 waves.

incident-bot: :rotating_light: Update 2155559000 - customer-facing errors reduced after batching toggle + canary patch. Still watching.

ryan: Wave 1 rollout to 30% of clusters started. I'm keeping continuous_batching off for those during rollout.

customer-success: Acme reports latencies returning to normal after our initial change. NovaHealth still seeing intermittent failures but much improved. They're asking for RCA ETA.

oncall-ml: Triage notes so far: root cause appears to be a combination of (1) batch-config change increased max_prefix_bytes + larger continuous batching window, which allowed a noisy tenant to fill KV cache with very large prefixes, and (2) allocator regression that allowed skewed shard assignment under high token_count, amplifying memory pressure on a subset of tensor-parallel ranks and triggering NCCL stalls.

eng-runtime: Agreed. Next steps: 
- ship allocator hotfix to all pools (kv_shard_allocator v1.0.1)
- revert risky batch-config defaults in config repo (revert: r-2026-03-12-77)
- add autosafe config: if kv_cache_size > X for 5m then auto-disable continuous_batching for that pool
- postmortem to include traffic sample from noisy tenant and test-case to reproduce skew

mike: Rolling revert of batch-config now (deploy id r-2026-03-12-77-rollback). This will set max_prefix_bytes back to 4MB and reduce continuous_batch_window to 30s.

ops-runbook-bot: Safety check: ensure min_capacity remains >= baseline when toggling batching to avoid SLA breaches for high QPS customers.

infra-shift-lead: Rollout of allocator patch wave 2 started. Expect 8-10m per wave. We'll pause if we see any CPU/oom regressions.

ryan: Wave 1 metrics: kv_page_fault_rate -60%, p50 token latency -30%, NCCL timeouts -> 0 in canary. Wave 2 in progress.

customer-success: Acme and NovaHealth Slack channels updated. Both appreciate the quick mitigation. Acme asked for timeline to fully remediate and a commitment on config defaults.

oncall-ml: Immediate mitigations complete: batching toggle + batch-config revert + allocator hotfix rollout. Current customer impact: reduced to informational (no active outages), some elevated error rates for a small slice of requests for 20 more minutes while waves finish.

incident-bot: :white_check_mark: Status 2155559145 - all production clusters show shard_balance_ratio < 1.5 and kv_cache_size trending down. No NCCL stalls reported in the last 10m. Incident downgraded to mitigated.

eng-runtime: Postmortem owners: sara (lead), mike (mitigation timeline), ryan (metrics + dashboards), eva (customer comms). Target initial draft in 48h. Action items: add unit test for shard allocator, add autosafe in control plane, revert-safe deploy gating for batch-config changes.

customer-success: We'll send a summary to Acme/NovaHealth tonight and offer technical debrief next week.

oncall-ml: Closing notes: if anyone sees reversion of kv.cache.max_prefix_bytes or sudden spike in kv_cache_size, page oncall-ml and eng-runtime immediately.

mike: I'll follow up with a short changelog and the rollback PR link: https://git.redwood/changes/r-2026-03-12-77-rollback

incident-bot: Incident 2155558888 - MITIGATED. Postmortem scheduled.
